original_question: Given a function f in D^alpha such that f does not have an analytic extension to the closed disk, find the rate of decay of ||q_n f - 1||_alpha.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the ambient quantity of interest—the decay of the optimal-approximant error ||q_n f - 1||_alpha in a Dirichlet-type space D_alpha—and it is aimed at the paper’s norm-convergence/open-problem discussion rather than its sections on zeros or digital filters.
missing_details: The paper’s official formulation puts the non-extension hypothesis on 1/f, not on f itself.
The symbol q_n must be defined: it is the n-th optimal polynomial approximant to 1/f, i.e. the polynomial of degree at most n minimizing ||p f - 1||_alpha over all polynomials p of degree at most n.
The question is meaningful only in the cyclic regime (or at least when ||q_n f - 1||_alpha -> 0); this cyclicity link is stated in the introduction.
The ambient space should be identified as the Dirichlet-type space D_alpha of analytic functions on the unit disk D, for a fixed real parameter alpha.
The closed disk should be written as the closed unit disk \overline{D}.
The asymptotic variable n -> infinity should be stated explicitly.
The degree restriction 'degree at most n' for q_n is implicit in the draft and needs to be made explicit.
An equivalent distance formulation is available in the paper: ||q_n f - 1||_alpha = dist_{D_alpha}(1, f P_n), where P_n is the space of polynomials of degree at most n.
The nearby context explains why this is the complementary case to the easier one: if 1/f extends analytically to \overline{D}, then the decay is exponential.
The paper presents this as an open question, not as a theorem with a known answer.
refined_question: Fix a real parameter alpha, and let D_alpha be the Dirichlet-type space on the unit disk D. For a cyclic function f in D_alpha, let q_n denote the n-th optimal polynomial approximant to 1/f; that is, q_n is the polynomial of degree at most n that minimizes ||p f - 1||_alpha over all p in P_n. Assuming that 1/f does not admit an analytic extension to the closed unit disk \overline{D}, what is the asymptotic rate, as n -> infinity, of the error ||q_n f - 1||_alpha?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, for such a cyclic f, determine the asymptotic behavior of dist_{D_alpha}(1, f P_n) as n -> infinity, where P_n is the space of polynomials of degree at most n.
justification: The draft is targeting the norm-decay problem in Section 5.1, and the nearest official formulation is exactly Open Question 5. However, the paper’s wording and preceding discussion show that the relevant obstruction is failure of analytic extension of the reciprocal 1/f to the closed disk, not of f itself. The introduction defines D_alpha and the n-th optimal polynomial approximant, and also states that f is cyclic if and only if ||q_n f - 1||_alpha -> 0, which is the hidden assumption needed for a genuine decay-rate question. The paragraph immediately preceding Open Question 5 explains that when 1/f does extend analytically to \overline{D}, the decay is exponential, so Open Question 5 asks for the complementary non-extendable case. The alternate formulation is paper-faithful because q_n f - 1 is exactly the optimal error for approximating 1 by elements of f P_n.
